logline: In 1880s New York, a penniless young woman navigates the bitter war between old-money Manhattan and the newly rich industrialists trying to buy their way into society.

renewal.note: Renewed for Season 4 in July 2025. The series has built critical momentum across each season, with Seasons 2 and 3 landing above 94% on Rotten Tomatoes.

bollymeter.basis: A 79% Rotten Tomatoes score and a 68 Metacritic rating reflect a solid but slightly cautious first season - critics admired the production design and Christine Baranski's commanding presence while finding the plotting crowded.

seasons.review_body: Julian Fellowes returned to the period drama he perfected with Downton Abbey and planted it in 1880s New York, where the tension between old Knickerbocker families and nouveau riche industrial wealth made for richer class conflict than the English upstairs-downstairs formula. Season 1 earned 79% on Rotten Tomatoes and a 68 Metacritic score - generally positive notices qualified by the observation that the pilot overloads its narrative with characters. Christine Baranski as the imperious Agnes van Rhijn and Carrie Coon as the social-climbing Bertha Russell are the central poles around which everything orbits. Louisa Jacobson as the naive newcomer Marian carries the audience-surrogate role with more grace than the dialogue always earns. The HBO production values - costuming, set design, location work in Newport - are immaculate.

episode_reviews.title: Never the New
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere introduces the full social battlefield across several households simultaneously. Fellowes trusts the viewer to sort the families and allegiances; the production design carries much of the orientation work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bertha Russell's first formal attempt at a society dinner invitation being returned without reply - the social humiliation that sets the series' central engine running.

bollymeter.basis: A 94% Rotten Tomatoes score represents a major critical leap from Season 1 - reviewers found the show had settled into its characters and delivered richer, more confident storytelling around Bertha Russell's social conquest.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 of The Gilded Age arrived in late 2023 to reviews that treated it as a different, superior show from its predecessor. The 94% Rotten Tomatoes score reflected critical consensus that Fellowes had found his rhythm and that Carrie Coon had elevated the entire production around her. Bertha Russell's social campaign in Season 2 is executed with strategic precision that gives the show its best scenes: the jockeying for opera box invitations, the alliances and betrayals among women who wield social exclusion like a weapon. The 73 Metacritic score confirmed the critical uplift as real. Season 2 Emmy nominations for Outstanding Drama Series signalled that HBO's bet on the series had paid off on the awards circuit as well.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 sheds the introductory clutter of the premiere year and focuses its energies: Bertha's social war is now in full swing, and Carrie Coon commands each scene she is in.

episode_reviews.title: In Terms of Winning
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The Season 2 finale resolves several social battles and opens new ones - it operates as a satisfying close to the season's main arcs without fully releasing the pressure that makes the show work.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bertha's triumph at the opera - the social coup she has been engineering all season finally executing, in a setting where the audience literally witnesses the hierarchy reshuffled.

bollymeter.basis: A 95-96% Rotten Tomatoes score and Emmy nominations for Outstanding Drama Series confirm Season 3 as the peak of the series to date - critics found the storytelling at its most assured and the performances at their most layered.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 arrived in summer 2025 to the strongest reviews the series has received. The near-perfect critical consensus (95-96% on Rotten Tomatoes) reflected a show that had fully grown into its ensemble and its setting. Christine Baranski's Agnes and Carrie Coon's Bertha have by Season 3 developed a complex adversarial-respectful dynamic that carries layers the first season could not have supported. The six Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Drama Series, placed The Gilded Age alongside HBO's most celebrated contemporary dramas. Fellowes's increasing confidence with American class anxiety sets Season 3 apart from the British model he built his career on - the transactional brutality of the Russell family's ascent hits differently than anything in Downton.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 represents the full maturation of the ensemble - the class warfare that felt plotted in Season 1 now feels lived-in, and the show earns its dramatic peaks rather than decorating them.
